title: Active-Passive DR Playbook, Backup/Restore Validation, and Quarterly Failover Drill
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create and validate an operator-friendly Active-Passive disaster recovery (DR) playbook for Redwood's inference control plane and serving runtime. This ticket covers: 1) formalized runbook for initiating scheduled and unscheduled active->passive failovers across regions, 2) backup and restore validation for critical state (deployment configs, model catalog metadata, KV caches/TTL snapshots where applicable, billing/usage ledger exports), 3) a scripted quarterly failover drill that exercises circuit breakers, load-shedding behaviors, and automated rollback, and 4) acceptance criteria tied to SLOs and observability checks. The playbook must include pre-flight checks, manual and automated steps, mitigation for partial failures, and clear post-drill validation tasks.
acceptance_criteria: A documented active-passive failover runbook stored in Confluence with step-by-step operator commands and expected outputs
A backup/restore validation checklist that can be executed non-destructively and in a staged environment
A drill plan for a quarterly scheduled failover including participants, timing, and communication templates
A post-drill report template that includes SLO impact, incident timelines, and action items
Automated verification scripts (CI) that validate that restored metadata leads to consistent routing decisions and model version pinning
Circuit breaker and load-shedding config matrix verified during drill with measured thresholds and telemetry captured
runbook: Scope: Control plane state (model catalog, rollout configs), route tables, regional traffic policies, and critical datastore snapshots (Postgres backups, S3 manifests). Serving runtime ephemeral state (KV cache) will be validated for impact only; full KV restore not required for scheduled drills.

Prep: Notify customers via status page draft, inform on-call and SRE rotation 72 hours prior, reserve maintenance windows in both primary and DR regions, ensure playbook and scripts are in repo infra/dr-playbooks.

Pre-flight checks: health of control plane, replication lag < 5s for primary replication, all scheduled jobs passing, backup manifests exist and pass checksum verification, current SLO burn rates under 10% for last 24h.

Failover (automated path): 1) Promote passive region read replica to primary via promote-replica script; 2) Switch traffic using smart-router to point to DR region with canary percentage at 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 15 minutes; 3) Apply model catalog read-only lock, verify rollouts and feature flags in new region; 4) Monitor SLOs and rollback if error rate > 2% or latency P95 > SLO threshold for > 10m.
Failover (manual path): Steps for manual failover when automation fails, including manual promotion commands, DNS TTL changes, and load balancer (LB) health-check overrides.

Rollback: Revert router to original region, demote promoted DB, re-sync any writes made to DR primary back to original primary using logical replication tooling. Maintain snd/rcv WAL segments and record timeline to avoid split-brain.

Post-failover verification: run smoke tests (tokenized inference paths, embeddings consistency checks), validate billing ledger continuity for last 24h, ensure console dashboards reflect correct region tags.

Communication: Templates for status page updates, customer email, and internal incident bridge notes. Escalation matrix to Eng Director and Head of Reliability if drill shows > 30m degradation or data loss risk.
backup_validation_steps: Daily logical backups: verify Parquet manifest and row counts for critical tables (deployments, model_versions, rollouts).
Weekly full snapshot: restore to staging cluster and run integration smoke tests for API compatibility and model pinning behavior.

Monthly: run simulated restore in isolated VPC with synthetic traffic (no customer data). Validate ordering guarantees for rollout IDs and that model weights references map to existing artifacts in object store.
KV cache sanity: export prefix cache manifests and validate cache-miss ratios after restore to ensure degradation within tolerated SLO delta.
Ledger continuity test: import last 48h billing/export into restored DB and run reconciliations to detect missing transactions.
Retention and encryption: ensure KMS-wrapped backups are decryptable by restore tooling and IAM roles are correct in DR region.
drill_plan: Schedule: Quarterly scheduled window (2 hours) in low-traffic slot; this ticket targets Apr 2 2026 for the first run.
Participants: SREs (on-call + backup), Platform Eng, Two service owners (API + Runtime), PM observer, Communications lead.
Objectives: Verify automated failover completes end-to-end, confirm circuit breakers trip and traffic is shed gracefully, validate rollback within SLA when injected failure causes SLO violations.
Success criteria: All critical endpoints respond within SLO targets after cutover OR safe rollback executed within 20 minutes with no data loss; manual restore path documented and rehearsed.
Failure modes to exercise: DB promotion fails, router cannot apply policy, LB health checks flapping, partial write divergence in DR primary.
Observability: Ensure logs forwarded to central ELK, traces sampled for 100% of drill traffic for first 30 minutes, and synthetic transactions emit custom drill tag 'drill-2026q2'.
circuit_breaker_and_load_shedding_matrix: Circuit breaker tiers: service-level (soft) trips at 5xx rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m; hard trips at 5% for 2m -> route to degraded model variant or capacity-tier fallback.
Load shedding policy: Shed non-critical batch and embedding requests first; enforce token-budget per-request ceilings for uncontrolled burst patterns.

Graceful degradation flow: On detection of backpressure in GPU pool, shift inference to lower-precision quantized variants with equivalent API surface and annotate responses with 'degraded_model' header.
Telemetry checks: Ensure circuit-breaker state, shed counts, and model-variant switches are emitted to metrics with drill tag for correlation.
post_drill_tasks: Complete post-drill report within 72 hours using template in Confluence: include timeline, SLO graphs, errors by code, and action items with owners.
Create follow-up tickets for gaps found (e.g., DB promotion script race condition, missing telemetry) and link as dependencies.
Update runbook with lessons learned and revise automated playbooks; add unit/integration tests to CI for restore path.
Schedule a cross-team review walk-through and tabletop for any data-loss or >20m outage scenarios.
